kinpaku-gold.description: The mark, the arrow in the primary button, the dot on an active instrument key, the gold underline on a selected tab, the Go and Accept fills in the picker. Under 2:1 against paper, so it never carries text there.

kinpaku-vivid.description: Lit hover on a gold fill.

kinpaku-pale.description: Pale gold tint; rarely needed on paper.

kinpaku-rich.description: Hairline gold on paper, the active rule. --ks-gold-line aliases it.

on-gold.description: The foreground on a gold fill (picker Go and Accept) and on the patina skip link.

gold-line.description: The one-pixel gold rule. Aliases kinpaku-rich. Use one, not a set.

patina.description: Indicator on instruments, the focus ring, the toggle when on, the skip link fill.

patina-pale.description: A soft fill behind a selected row.

patina-deep.description: Patina as text: links, the selected tab, .is-improved and .is-ready badges, the ghost button on hover. Clears 4.5:1 on paper. Reached through --ks-accent-ink, --ks-state-ink and --ks-link-on-paper.

patina-ink.description: Hover on patina text. --ks-link-on-paper-hover aliases it.

link-line.description: The underline under a link on paper: patina-deep at 40%. The ramp shows the base color.

vermilion.description: .is-detected, the warning toast, the picker's exit and discard hovers. Failures and warnings only.

paper.description: The page ground. A hair below white so a raised card can read as raised. Chroma 0.

paper-raised.description: Cards, panels, inputs, the secondary button, the segmented thumb, the GitHub pill.

paper-deep.description: Sunk wells, code blocks, the segmented track, the footer, tooltips.

gray.description: Chips, inactive fills, inline code, the toggle at rest, the secondary button on press.

paper-veil.description: Kit literal, not a token: the sticky header, paper at 92% over a 12px blur. The only translucency on the site.

instrument.description: The face of a strip, a terminal, a picker bar. The only place the site goes dark.

instrument-deep.description: A track, a well, the strip's border.

instrument-raised.description: A key cap, a thumb, the active picker toggle.

instrument-muted.description: Muted text on instruments; an instrument key at rest.

instrument-rule.description: Divider and the inset highlight along the top of an instrument face. White at 12%; the ramp shows the neutral base.

instrument-edge.description: The inset top edge on an active key. White at 30%; the ramp shows the neutral base.

ink.description: Headlines, <strong>, active nav, and the fill of the primary button. --ks-nav-active aliases it.

text.description: Body copy; also the primary button's hover fill in the kit.

text-muted.description: Captions, meta, eyebrows, section subheads, nav links at rest, footer links.

text-faint.description: Subdued meta, segmented labels at rest, counts.

text-mute-deep.description: Disabled only. Measures under 4.5:1 on paper by design; a live figure using it is a bug.

rule.description: Divides content. Ink at 12%; does not clear 3:1, so it never bounds a control. The ramp shows the base.

edge.description: Bounds something you can operate. Ink at 45%, clears 3:1 for WCAG 1.4.11. The ramp shows the base.

wordmark.purpose: IMPECCABLE in the header lockup and the footer logo. The only place Alumni Sans appears; part of the logo, not a display face.

display.purpose: Page h1. Albert Sans at 500; never 100 or 300.

headline.purpose: Section h2. The kit styles any h2 inside .ks-section-head to this role.

title.purpose: Card and panel headings, h3. Albert Sans at 600.

body.purpose: Long copy at line-height 1.65. Holds a 65ch measure.

control.purpose: Button labels. A .ks-button literal: the ui-lead size at 500, line-height 1.

eyebrow.purpose: Small mono caps above titles. Color is text-muted, not gold and not patina. Short labels only, never a sentence.

micro.purpose: Dense ramp floor (11px). Nothing functional goes below it.

label.purpose: Control text and caps section heads (12px). Instrument keys and segmented controls set this size in the mono family.

ui.purpose: List rows and any sentence someone reads to make a decision (13px). The --lg segmented variant uses it in the reading face.

ui-lead.purpose: Top of the dense ramp (15px); the size the button label borrows.

small.purpose: Reading ramp (14px): secondary body copy and captions that are read rather than scanned.

subhead.purpose: Reading ramp (20px): a card-level heading at 500.

title-lg.purpose: Reading ramp (24px): a bento tile or panel heading that is larger than a card title but not a section.

shadows.name: ks-lift-1
shadows.purpose: A raised card, the segmented thumb, the instrument strip on the paper.

shadows.name: ks-lift-2
shadows.purpose: A popover, a modal, a picker bar. No default card shadow: cards and tiles rest on --ks-rule and a surface step.

motion.name: ks-ease
motion.purpose: The one curve, for both durations. Declare the transition once per surface.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Below it the header's nav and GitHub pill collapse into a drawer behind .site-header-menu.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Below it bento tiles collapse to full width.

controlHeights.name: ks-control-sm
controlHeights.purpose: Dense chrome in a rail; the --dense segmented variant.

controlHeights.name: ks-control-md
controlHeights.purpose: The default: instrument keys and the segmented control. A segmented track lands here by construction (3px inset, 24px segment, 3px, two borders).

sm.purpose: Buttons, inputs, chips and the segmented track.

md.purpose: Cards, the picker bar and its command palette.

pill.purpose: The instrument strip and its keys, the toggle, tags, the GitHub pill.

nested.purpose: Derived geometry, not a fourth radius: a control nested inside another subtracts 1px from its parent (the segmented thumb is 2px inside a 3px track; the --lg variant is 6px inside 8px).

narrative.overview:
The site is a vessel for the design Impeccable produces. Every world card, case study, slop specimen and live demo on it arrives with its own loud visual system, so the chrome has one job: get out of the way. A gallery wall is white so the art can be loud. The page is neutral paper, the type is ink in one family, and the brand shows up as jewelry rather than upholstery: a gold mark in the header, a one-pixel gold rule, a gold dot on a dark control.

This replaces the dark Neo Kinpaku system. No lacquer ground, no gold-leaf texture, no kintsugi hero art, no theme toggle. The proof still has to work: comparisons, command demos, audit tables and docs modules carry the color now, and the chrome around them stays quiet so they can.

site/styles/kinpaku-tokens.css names three families of surface: Paper, the page and everything that sits flat on it. Gray, chips, inactive fills, sunk wells. Instrument, dark control surfaces: the only place the site goes dark, and the only place gold reads as a signal rather than a mark.
keyCharacteristics: One light theme. `:root` sets `color-scheme: light`; there is no `html.dark`, no `prefers-color-scheme` block, no toggle.
Paper is neutral, chroma 0. Gold on cream is gold on gold.
Gold never carries text and never fills an area on paper.
Patina carries links, state and selection wherever color has to be read as text.
One family, Albert Sans, at 400 to 600. Alumni Sans exists for the wordmark and nothing else.
Three radii, three control heights, two lifts. Nothing else casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Kit Consumption Rule
rules.body: Reach for a kit primitive before inventing a class. Buttons: `.ks-button` plus a variant (`.ks-button-primary`, `-secondary`, `-ghost`, `-disabled`). Both classes are required; the chained selector is what beats page-level anchor resets. Do not write another `.hero-cta` or `.footer-cta`. Grouping content: `.ks-bento` with `.ks-bento-tile` (`--span-4` / `--span-6` / `--span-8` on a 12-column grid). This is the answer to "how do I group 2 to 6 items without nesting cards". Section scaffolding: `.ks-section` as the container, `.ks-section-head` for the header with an `<h2>` inside it (the kit styles it to the headline role), `.ks-section-sub` for the subhead. `.ks-section-eyebrow` above the h2 is optional; skip it on editorial pages where an eyebrow on every section reads as scaffolding. Anything the reader operates: `.ks-instrument-strip` for a dark tab strip or command switcher, `.ks-segmented` for a paper single-select. Do not build a fifth segmented control; the kit's exists because five bespoke ones did. Status, tags, toasts, modals, tooltips, empty states, pagination, skeletons, changelog rows: the kit primitive. Invent only when the kit truly does not cover the shape, and flag it when you do. A pattern that solves a recurring need belongs in the kit, not in page CSS. Page CSS is for page-specific scenery.

rules.name: The Gold Is Jewelry Rule
rules.body: Gold is a mark, a line, or an indicator on an instrument. It never carries text at any size and never fills a surface on paper. The primary button is ink with a gold arrow; a gold button is the hotel-lobby read. The one exception is a demo that deliberately shows someone else's design.

rules.name: The Patina Carries Text Rule
rules.body: When color has to be read as text, it is `--ks-patina-deep`, reached through `--ks-accent-ink`, `--ks-state-ink` or `--ks-link-on-paper`. Active nav is ink, not patina, and eyebrows are muted ink.

rules.name: The Instruments Only Rule
rules.body: A dark surface is a control the reader operates: a tab strip, a segmented picker, a slider, a terminal, the live picker bar. No dark section backgrounds, no dark cards, no dark footer.

rules.name: The Neutral Paper Rule
rules.body: Every paper and ink token is chroma 0. Do not reintroduce a warm cast.

rules.name: The Tokens Over Literals Rule
rules.body: New colors are `--ks-*` tokens in OKLCH. A literal is a one-off alpha of a token or a specimen of someone else's design.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Alumni Sans is part of the logo, not a display face. If a heading wants a condensed face, it wants the wrong thing.

rules.name: The No Hairline Rule
rules.body: Display and headline sit at 500, titles at 600. Never 100 or 300 on a heading; those were the condensed face's weights and Albert Sans at 300 is not even loaded.

rules.name: The Micro Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing functional goes below 11px. Being on the ramp does not exempt a value; 10px fails on high-DPI and on small viewports whatever the token is called.

rules.name: The Tracked Labels Are Short Rule
rules.body: Tracked mono caps are for eyebrows, section labels and tile numbers. Never a sentence.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: A 1px `--ks-rule` before any shadow. `--ks-edge` when the line bounds something operable.

rules.name: The One Veil Rule
rules.body: The sticky header is paper at 92% over a 12px blur. That is the only translucency on the site; there are no glass panels.

rules.name: The No Texture Rule
rules.body: No leaf, dust, grain, seam or oxidation images anywhere in the chrome. Depth is geometry.

rules.name: The Three-Radius Rule
rules.body: Use `--ks-radius-sm`, `--ks-radius-md` or `--ks-radius-pill`. Treat a nested-control subtraction as derived geometry, not a fourth radius. The older kit primitives (inputs, checkbox, badge, toast, tooltip, modal, pagination, empty state) still carry a literal 2px; when one is touched, it moves to the token.

dos: Do keep the chrome quiet so the demos can be loud.
Do put gold on the mark, a one-pixel rule, or an indicator on an instrument.
Do use `--ks-accent-ink`, `--ks-state-ink` or `--ks-link-on-paper` whenever color has to be read as text.
Do reserve `--ks-instrument*` for something the reader operates.
Do set headings in Albert Sans at 500 and 600 through the type tokens.
Do land every radius, control height and shadow on the ladder.
Do reach for the kit primitive first, and flag it when a new pattern earns a place in the kit.
Do keep the proof readable: comparisons, sliders, audit tables, command examples and docs are the product.
donts: Do not add a dark mode, a theme toggle, an `html.dark` selector or a `prefers-color-scheme` block.
Do not set gold as a text color, at any size, on paper.
Do not fill a button, chip, slab or panel with gold on paper.
Do not give a decorative section, card or footer a dark background.
Do not tint paper or ink; every surface and text token is chroma 0.
Do not use Alumni Sans outside the wordmark, or weight 100 or 300 anywhere.
Do not add a fourth radius, a fourth control height or a third shadow.
Do not hand-type an `oklch()` value in page CSS except as a one-off alpha of a token or inside a specimen of someone else's design.
Do not use pure black or pure white.
Do not theme-adapt the live picker to a host page.
